profile.reading: This building at 3101 Western Avenue in Seattle, Washington, a seven story office building dating to 1984 in the Belltown neighborhood near Elliott Bay, is identified by the name CTI Biopharma, a real biopharmaceutical company that was headquartered in Seattle. CTI Biopharma developed treatments for hematologic cancers, cancers of the blood and bone marrow, and brought its lead drug pacritinib, sold under the brand name Vonjo, to market for myelofibrosis, a rare bone marrow disorder. In 2023 the Swedish pharmaceutical company Sobi, Swedish Orphan Biovitrum, acquired CTI Biopharma, and CTI Biopharma's own former website now forwards visitors to Sobi's American site. Companies like this maintain corporate offices and laboratories with their own internal IT infrastructure, a server closet or small equipment room supporting business systems, email, and research computing, which is a different use case from a commercial data center that leases space, power, and connectivity to outside customers. Nothing found about CTI Biopharma or its acquisition by Sobi suggests the company ever operated a colocation or wholesale data center business at this or any other address. This entry is filed as an honest correction rather than padded with unrelated data center detail. The building is corporate office and laboratory space belonging to a life sciences company, not a commercial data center.

reading.body:
This entry is a correction. The building at 3101 Western Avenue in Seattle is the former corporate headquarters and research laboratory of CTI Biopharma, a biopharmaceutical company acquired by Swedish Orphan Biovitrum in 2023. It is not a commercial data center.

The structure is a seven-story office building from 1984 in Belltown. Companies of this type maintain internal IT infrastructure for business systems and research computing, which differs fundamentally from a colocation facility that leases space, power, and connectivity to outside customers. No published evidence suggests CTI Biopharma operated a wholesale data center business at this address or elsewhere.

This campus publishes no power specifications and holds no rank in the state's published capacity. Washington state has 46 mapped facilities in this site's database, only two of which have published megawatt figures totaling 60 MW. This entry does not contribute to that count.
